name: OS Command Injection
description: OS Command Injection occurs when untrusted user input is incorporated into an operating system command without adequate validation or safe command construction. An attacker may manipulate the input to execute unintended commands with the privileges of the vulnerable application.
common_causes: Passing user-controlled input directly to operating system command execution functions
Using subprocess functions with shell=True and untrusted input
Constructing shell commands through string concatenation
Constructing shell commands using f-strings or format()
Failing to separate command arguments from user-controlled data
vulnerable_patterns: subprocess.run() used with shell=True and untrusted input
subprocess.Popen() used with shell=True and untrusted input
Shell commands constructed using string concatenation
User-controlled input passed directly to command execution

vulnerable_examples.explanation: The user-controlled input is passed directly to os.system(), allowing the input to influence the operating system command.
The command is interpreted by a shell while containing user-controlled input, creating a command injection risk.
User-controlled hostname data is concatenated into a shell command before execution.

secure_patterns: Avoid shell command execution when a library or Python API can perform the required operation
Pass command arguments as a list rather than constructing a shell command string
Use an allowlist for permitted commands or arguments
Avoid passing untrusted input directly to shell interpreters

secure_examples.explanation: The command and its argument are supplied separately without invoking a shell.
Command arguments are represented as separate list elements and shell interpretation is disabled.

detection_indicators: shell=True is used with externally controlled data
Command strings are constructed using string concatenation
Command strings are constructed using f-strings
Command strings are constructed using format()
External input is passed to a shell command without strict validation
remediation: Avoid shell command execution when possible. When subprocess execution is necessary, prefer shell=False and pass commands and arguments as separate elements in a list. Validate or allowlist externally supplied arguments and avoid constructing shell command strings from untrusted input.

references.title: MITRE CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet
